_README: Pin registry for the bridge soundness guard (proofs/proof_guard.py).
`core_modules` — the ONLY module roots whose constants may go unpinned: core
Lean, fixed by proofs/lean-toolchain. The guard's audit scope is the
COMPLEMENT of this allowance, computed from the kernel environment. It used
to be the other way round — a constant counted only if its owning module was
listed in a front's `build` — so deleting one module name from `build`
silently unpinned everything it owned, with no message and no claim covering
it (2026-07 round-4 review, F17).
`fronts` — one entry per bridge: which modules it builds (`build`, the one
place the compiled set is spelled; the bridges compile exactly this), which
modules the environment query loads (`modules`, a subset of `build`), which
sources the textual/denylist layer audits (strict = model files, and every
strict source must be a built module; runner = the *Run.lean I/O plumbing,
where `partial` is allowed), which axioms that front's documented TCB permits
(proofs/README.md), which of its theorems may additionally rest on
`native_decide` trust axioms (`native_decide_ok`) and which declarations may
GENERATE those axioms (`native_decide_sources` — each is queried and
statement-pinned like a guarded theorem, because a trust axiom was previously
accepted on its shape alone, from any declaration, pinned or not: round-4,
F20), and the guarded theorem list itself.
`statements` — the canonical dump of each guarded theorem's ELABORATED type
(binder NAMES and mdata dropped, binder ANNOTATIONS and universe parameters
kept; structural, not pretty-printed, so no notation or delaborator can
change it; string literals by CONTENT, as hex of their UTF-8 bytes). The
guard compares the environment's answer against this string: axiom-cone
checking alone certified `theorem memory_bound : True := trivial` as clean
(2026-07 round-2 review, F1), a length-only literal dump left every genesis
hash pin free to name a different object (round-3, F13), and dropping binder
info let `(w : W) (h : Valid w)` and `{w : W} ⦃h : Valid w⦄` dump identically
(round-4, F19). A drift is a hard failure with a diff.
`definitions` — every constant the queried statements' MEANING rests on: the
type AND value of each definition, the type AND constructor list of each
inductive. The set is computed from the kernel environment (the constants in
a theorem's type, then transitively through the definitions those mention),
never hand-listed, and a member without a pin is a hard failure — so a new
dependency cannot appear silently. Statement pins alone let `Reach` lose its
recursive constructor and `Valid` become `False` with every dump unchanged
and every bridge green (round-3, F12). Dumps over 4000 chars (the 200 KB
`lutString`, `Sha256.sha256`) are pinned by `sha256:<hex>:<len>` of the same
dump: identical content, only the diff's readability differs.
`unguarded` — theorems deliberately NOT axiom-cone-checked, with the reason.
Every theorem in proofs/*.lean must appear here or in a front's guarded list,
so adding one is a deliberate act (a new poisoned theorem in a guarded file
used to be invisible to the guard). Anonymous `example`s are rejected
outright: nothing can query them. Entries here must ALSO appear in the
reviewed allowlist in proofs/GUARD_CLAIMS.txt, which additionally names — by
identity, not by count — every guarded theorem, every native_decide source,
each front's build/modules/sources/axioms, the core-module allowance, and
this file's content hash. Without it the registry authorizes itself
(round-3, F14); with counts alone a demotion was a one-line hash diff
(round-4, F18).
To change a statement legitimately: edit the proof, run
`python3 proofs/proof_guard.py regen`, and review the diff as carefully as
you would review the theorem statement — this file is the claim.
